description_html:
Goodfire technical staff member Curt Tigges discusses research revealing that individual MLP neurons in modern language models are far more interpretable and functionally bounded than previously thought. Using an automated agent to test hypotheses across architectures like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Tigges explains how modern gated MLPs act as legible conjunctions and control signals capable of extensive dynamic sparsity without lasting benchmark loss. By showing that many internal representations can be directly enumerated, this work offers an alternative to complex external featurizers and provides practical avenues for behavior monitoring and persona steering.

For full show notes, links, and references, read the episode page:https://www.cognitiverevolution.ai/the-neuron-basis-goodfire-s-curt-tigges-on-agentic-interp-monosemanticity-reverse-engineering/
